other_up.note:
Not "no bound": an exponential one. A decision tree of depth $\mathrm{D}$ has at
most $2^{\mathrm{D}}-1$ internal nodes, hence queries at most that many distinct
variables; reading all of them non-adaptively determines the whole path, and with
it the tree's output. Nothing here is specific to Boolean output, so it holds for
relations.

other_lo.note: The exponential bound is attained exactly, with no constant to spare: binary tree navigation has $\mathrm{D}=k$ and all $2^k-1$ variables relevant.

facts: Adaptivity can save exponentially: $\mathrm{D}(\mathrm{ADDR}) = \log_2 n + 1$ while $\mathrm{D}^{\mathrm{na}}(\mathrm{ADDR}) = n + \log_2 n$, since every data bit is relevant.

The other direction is exponential, not unbounded: $\mathrm{D}^{\mathrm{na}}(f) \le 2^{\mathrm{D}(f)}-1$, since a depth-$\mathrm{D}$ tree has at most that many internal nodes and so touches at most that many variables. Binary tree navigation $\mathrm{Nav}_k$ attains it exactly.
$\mathrm{D}^{\mathrm{na}}(f) \ge \mathrm{s}(f)$, $\mathrm{bs}(f)$, $\mathrm{deg}(f)$ and every other measure, since all of them are supported on relevant variables.
self.name: Non-adaptive deterministic query complexity
self.short: Fewest queries when the whole query set must be fixed in advance.
